record.title: Match adjusted event-time hazards to a model

cues.phrase: a treatment hazard ratio that is constant over follow-up / an adjusted treatment hazard ratio / Cox proportional-hazards regression
cues.why: The previous exact 'proportional hazards' phrase has been removed from the stem, but 'hazard ratio' still occurs twice and only the key contains the word root 'hazard'. Covering the statistical meaning still permits a stem-to-option word match. The requested hazard ratio is legitimate task information; the avoidable cue is retaining that root only in the keyed option's expanded model name.

fairness: The prior suggested opening was implemented: independent censoring and a treatment hazard ratio constant over follow-up replace the named proportional-hazards assumption. The exact-phrase problem is repaired, but the broader wording-only shortcut remains.

Cox regression is the unique best listed model for the adjusted hazard ratio for time to recurrence under the stated assumptions. Binary logistic regression and multiple linear regression are reasonable outcome-type misconceptions, not equally correct answers.

The explanation accurately connects Cox regression with adjusted event-time hazard ratios, proportional hazards and appropriately independent censoring. No clinical or statistical key error is identified.

This is a high-yield, easy model-selection recall item, and it need not acquire a second step. Its standalone task and supplied assumptions are clear. REVISE is solely for the residual lexical cue, not ease, missing clinical detail or failure to be two-step.
suggestions: Use the conventional option label 'Cox regression' alongside 'Binary logistic regression' and 'Multiple linear regression'. Keep the hazard-ratio objective and stated assumptions in the task, and keep the full 'Cox proportional-hazards regression' name in post-answer feedback. This removes the unique shared word root without obscuring necessary statistical information.

record.title: Administrative access for referral scheduling

cues.phrase: confirm the phone number and book the named receiving clinic
cues.why: The task is decomposed into two facts, each assigned to one document. Matching labels gives the key without privacy knowledge.
Complete makes this the obvious overbroad choice in a minimum-information exercise.

fairness: Registration and the referral order suffice for the limited assignment. Ability to open other documents does not establish work-related need.
Keep feedback about this assignment, not a claim that schedulers can never need pathology or that this administrative restriction governs clinician-to-clinician treatment disclosures.

No confident privacy-rule error identified. This is elementary document selection rather than a high-yield resident confidentiality decision; highYield is false for this exact objective, not confidentiality generally.
The named employee retains her work role and the patient has a coherent clinic frame.
suggestions: Consolidate or explicitly accept as workforce onboarding if retaining this administrative objective.
For boards-oriented supply, test a consequential confidentiality decision within the surgeon’s responsibility with credible competing disclosures and specified purpose/recipient.
Do not hide the actual assignment or grant clinical duties to the scheduler merely to increase difficulty.

record.title: Scope disclosure for an imminent threat

cues.phrase: information to identify and intercept him
cues.why: The stated task makes an identity-containing answer mandatory before privacy reasoning begins. This is a legitimate response need, but the option set then supplies a competitor that explicitly defeats it.

cues.phrase: Send the intended victim’s details while withholding the speaker’s identity
cues.why: The while-withholding clause advertises the very omission that prevents the stated identification/interception task. It is a self-disqualifying distractor, not a neutral competing disclosure scope.

cues.phrase: a focused account of the threatened attack
cues.why: Focused marks the key as the tailored middle option between a clinic chart and explicitly withheld identity. Once the withholding foil is eliminated, the wording favors the key without applying the HIPAA exception.

fairness: Prior fairness[0-2] and suggestion[1]: the target, means, timing, clinician assessment and emergency response remain clear. Identity plus necessary threat information is the single best offered disclosure. The explanation correctly separates HIPAA permission from local warning/reporting duties; no confident clinical or legal inaccuracy is asserted.

Prior cues[1-2] and suggestion[0] are only partly repaired. The admission and written-authorization prerequisites are gone, but an equally transparent obstacle remains in the explicitly anonymized interception option. Changing delay barriers to a withheld-identity barrier does not fully resolve the nonmedical cue problem.

Prior cue[0]: the clinician's good-faith assessment is retained in different words. That is legitimate context for the permission rule and is not itself a revision reason. Prior suggestion[2] is addressed: the unnecessary announcement of an information-sharing exercise is gone.
This is high-yield but easy single-rule confidentiality practice, with no second consequential inference. REVISE is for the self-defeating distractor and evaluative key wording, not for being easy.
suggestions: Keep the imminent threat and police response need. Compare neutral, similarly specific disclosure packages or recipients that can all plausibly support protective action; do not make one option deliberately prevent identifying the person officers must intercept.

Remove the evaluative focused qualifier and the while-withholding critique. Name the actual information included in each package. Let the resident apply relevance and permissible scope rather than recognize the only non-self-defeating middle option.

record.title: Operative access after failed peristomal mobilization
clarityIssues: The task asks which approach to select although the update is already intraoperative and documents substantial local dissection. Asking for the next operative step would locate the decision more precisely.

cues.phrase: the surgeon circumferentially freed the conduit and mobilized below the fascia
cues.why: Together with the stated failure to deliver bowel, this makes the peristomal mobilization option read as repetition of the failed maneuver. A test-wise reader can favor the only broader access route without resolving two competing surgical inferences.

cues.phrase: healthy bowel could not be delivered to skin level
cues.why: This explicitly supplies the access limitation. It is necessary operative information, but with two remaining local approaches it nearly finishes the reasoning before the options; do not manufacture difficulty by deleting a true operative finding.

fairness: Laparotomy with adhesiolysis and rematuration is a defensible best listed answer after documented unsuccessful local delivery of healthy bowel. The criticism is discrimination, not a confident clinical error in that key.

The deep scar map adds little independent difficulty once failed local mobilization and fixed intra-abdominal loops are supplied. Cutaneous advancement does not address the documented deep conduit problem; another peristomal plan is already strongly undermined by the completed attempt.

This is a high-yield stoma-revision principle, but the current item tests one escalation rule rather than two consequential steps. It is a standalone case and has no dependence on the separate superficial-stenosis case.
suggestions: Ask for the next step during the operation and distinguish the completed dissection from any genuinely untried procedure.

Replace the already-failed or anatomically inadequate alternatives with actual remaining operative choices, supplying only the supported patient-specific findings needed to rank them. If no credible remaining competition exists, seek explicit acceptance as a basic escalation item rather than claiming difficult two-step reasoning.

record.title: Elective repair of a symptomatic permanent-stoma hernia
fairness: Mesh-reinforced repair at the existing site is a defensible best general elective strategy among these choices. Primary suture repair and relocation with tissue repair are recognizable alternatives, but the main discrimination is recall of the usual repair principle.

The lead-in already fixes both elective timing and the diagnosis. Every option performs an operation and retains diversion. Consequently, deciding whether to operate and whether diversion remains necessary does not change which option wins; the removed rectum/anus cannot supply a second scored inference in this option set.
The recovered function and absence of an acute complication appropriately establish the setting. They should not be counted as additional reasoning steps merely because they are present.

No strong wording-only cue or confident clinical error identified. This is a high-yield but easy standalone rule-application item, not the requested difficult two-step question. The explanation should not be read as a universal prohibition on relocation in other anatomy.
suggestions: Make a real remaining patient-specific decision change the operation selected, using supported observations and clinically credible alternatives at the same stage. Do not add reversal as a disposable foil after explicitly removing the anorectal outlet.

If the learning objective remains simply mesh versus tissue repair, seek explicit acceptance as a basic item and trim details that do not affect that comparison. Do not label the current version moderate or two-step.

record.title: Seek independent evidence in the retained-gauze audit

cues.why: The task favors the only comparison that leaves the set of mutually compared documents. With the provenance table hidden, the physical-item option still stands out against two document-total reconciliations; ordinary test-taking can select the novel evidence type without interpreting which records copied which source.

cues.phrase: Check physical-item handling against the count board
cues.why: Only the key introduces physical handling. Both distractors compare totals among the transfer note, closure form and board. This retains a key-only novelty/medium cue even though the old cautious-versus-certain wording has been repaired.

fairness: The supplied table supports the intended answer: copied and read-back board entries do not independently verify a physical count. No confident clinical or causal inaccuracy identified.

Prior notes partly addressed: all choices are bounded audit plans, the two principal-cause overclaims are gone, and frozen uncertainty feedback no longer directly contradicts the distractors. The requested hide-the-table/independent-information check is not adequately repaired because the key is still the sole new evidence type.

The local update and table stand alone and follow error disclosure coherently. Independent defenses are high-yield, but this candidate bypasses the proposed provenance inference. REVISE is for the remaining cue, not for being easy.
suggestions: For any separately authorized future replacement, compare equally concrete and equally novel audit sources, with visible provenance distinguishing an independent observation from another source-dependent observation. The table, rather than a physical-versus-document label contrast, should determine the answer.
Apply the manager's single-fix-round disposition: drop this returned candidate from acceptance. Do not edit the frozen disclosure companion or start another repair round under this review.

record.title: Explicitly accept ownership of a pending culture
clarityIssues: The requested scope is 'obtaining it, interpreting it and deciding any response', but the key says only 'I accept culture interpretation and the clinical decision'. It does not explicitly accept obtaining/tracking the still-pending result. In a question specifically testing explicit ownership, accepting interpretation after receipt is not unambiguously the whole requested transfer.
fairness: Prior overstatement is repaired: the task asks which reply accepts the requested scope, not which sentence completes an entire handoff. The explanation appropriately preserves the need for clinical summary, follow-up expectations and contingencies.

The feasibility sentence and unrelated tissue-report distraction are removed; all options now expressly accept some work. The intended key is clearly better than transmission or scheduling for another clinician, but its omitted result-acquisition responsibility leaves a consequential ownership gap that the explanation fills only after answering.

This is an easy, high-yield safety rule and need not become two-step. REVISE concerns precision of the promised transfer, not difficulty. The standalone presentation and task otherwise identify the patient, pending culture and sender's continuing responsibility clearly.
suggestions: In any future authorized version, explicitly include tracking/obtaining the pending result together with interpretation and the response decision in the accepting plan; alternatively establish result acquisition as shared agreed context before testing the remaining clinical responsibility. Keep the options comparably specific.
Apply the single-fix-round rule and drop this returned candidate from acceptance; this review does not authorize another repair round.

record.title: Select a sample covering both actual contexts

cues.phrase: Both usual and relief staffing must be represented.
cues.why: The entire selection rule is given verbatim; the task only requires finding one row of each label.
The only mixed-label pair is selected by simple visual matching, without understanding sampling or quality improvement.

fairness: A/B is uniquely correct for the literal coverage requirement. C/D and E/F each cover one staffing category, and the explanation correctly avoids claiming representativeness from two observations.

Despite being fair at that elementary level, this does not test a meaningful resident statistical or surgical skill. The single-skill statistics exception permits brevity and ease, not replacing a testable method with arbitrary letter matching.
The cases and labels are clear; ambiguity is not the reason for failure. No second step should be added merely to inflate difficulty.
suggestions: Retire or merge this exact exercise rather than polish its labels.

If sampling needs coverage, replace it with one concise, high-yield decision about sampling bias, random selection within groups or what a sample can support, using credible alternatives and the minimum necessary data.
